title: What to expect: coronary CT angiogram

slides.title: A clear look at your heart's arteries.
Before your heart CT
items: Skip caffeine for 24 hours: coffee, tea, soda, energy drinks.
No heavy meal for 4 hours. Clear liquids are usually fine.
Keep taking your heart medicines unless we tell you otherwise.
Take Viagra, Cialis or similar? Skip it 24 to 48 hours before, and tell us.
slides.footnote: Sources: ACR/RSNA RadiologyInfo; NIH MedlinePlus. Follow the prep we give you when you book.

slides.title: How your visit goes.
steps: A small IV for contrast, and stickers on your chest to time the scan to your heartbeat.
If your heart is beating fast, you may get a medicine to slow it for sharper pictures.
Hold your breath for a few seconds. About 45 minutes start to finish.

slides.title: Quick and normal.
items: A brief warm, flushed feeling as the contrast goes in.
Maybe a metallic taste. It fades in seconds.
A short, open ring, not a long tunnel.
Back to your usual day right after.
slides.footnote: Tell us about a contrast allergy, kidney problems, diabetes or pregnancy. Source: NIH MedlinePlus.

slides.title: Simple to book in Seminole.
slides.footnote: Add Cleerly AI plaque analysis: $1,399 self-pay. With insurance, a doctor's order is needed and we check your benefits first. HSA/FSA receipts available.

slides.title: See your arteries, not just a number.
slides.share: Send this to someone with a heart CT coming up.
slides.disclaimer: General information, not medical advice. Chest pain now? Call 911. Self-pay prices as of November 2026. Using Medicare or Medicaid? Ask us what applies.

Have a coronary CT angiogram (heart CT) coming up? Here's what to expect at Advanced Medical Imaging in Seminole. Skip caffeine for 24 hours and avoid a heavy meal for 4 hours before; clear liquids are usually fine, and keep taking your heart medicines unless we tell you otherwise. If you take Viagra, Cialis or a similar medicine, skip it for 24 to 48 hours before and let us know. At your visit, a small IV is placed for contrast and stickers on your chest time the scan to your heartbeat. If your heart rate is fast, you may be given medicine to slow it for sharper pictures. The scan itself takes seconds while you hold your breath, and the whole visit is about 45 minutes. A warm, flushed feeling or a metallic taste from the contrast is normal and fades quickly. Tell us about any contrast allergy, kidney problems, diabetes or pregnancy. Self-pay coronary CTA is $395 with the radiologist's reading included, no referral needed, and appointments are usually available within a few days.
